key_insight: Reward-wise normalization can still leave sparse objectives underpowered; DARA fixes this by upweighting rewards that are active in fewer rollout groups using an inverse-square-root density correction.
engineering_relevance: For multi-reward RL systems, DARA offers a simple batch-level weighting rule that improves learning balance across objectives without changing the underlying policy optimization objective.
method: Measure each reward’s active-group density from the current rollout batch.
Use the density to compute an inverse-square-root correction for reward aggregation.
Reweight rewards adaptively during training while preserving GDPO-style reward-wise normalization.
evidence_signal: On tool calling, DARA reached high format compliance up to 26% fewer training steps than GDPO, and on mathematical reasoning it reached near-saturated length compliance up to 65% fewer steps while remaining competitive in final performance.
watch_item: Because weights are computed from each rollout batch, performance may depend on stable density estimates and could be sensitive when reward activity is very noisy or extremely rare.
paper_title: Make Sparse Rewards Count: Density-Aware Reward Aggregation for Multi-Reward RL
